Hi Stephanie — thanks for the grid and the clear asks. A few notes from the AWS side: 

1) SKU granularity: for co-sell + transactable SaaS offers we typically recommend one Offer per pricing model (so one offer per tier) to keep things simple for customers. You can add regional pricing via the Offer/Plan APIs rather than creating separate SKUs per region.

2) Certification & timeline: Expect 4–6 weeks for a standard transactable listing if you have all legal and security docs ready. If you want co-sell review (AWS AM approval) that can add another 2–3 weeks — plan for ~6–9 weeks total from submission.

3) Technical/collateral: we need a working set of SSO/OIDC details (SP-initiated), sample SAML metadata if you support it, a short integration runbook (3–4 pages), and a security checklist (SOC2/SCC/pen test summary). The Marketplace team will require a product brief and customer-facing listing copy.

4) Region guidance: canary in us-east-1 is fine. If latency-sensitive, consider us-west-2 as a second canary for west-coast customers.

I'll loop in our co-sell AM if we move forward — happy to fast-track once we have the legal bundle.

Cheers,
Priya Sharma
Senior Partner GTM Manager, AWS Marketplace

Thanks Stephanie — good outline. A few callouts from Azure Marketplace: 

- Offer types: Azure supports SaaS Offers (recommended for Redwood) and VM/Managed App images. For most of our customers, a SaaS transactable offer with meter-based plans works best.
- SKU versus plan: Azure expects a single Offer and then Plans for each sku/tier (so mapping Starter/Scale/Enterprise to Plans is the easiest path).
- Certification: Azure certification and transactable listing generally take 3–5 weeks; co-sell onboarding with a field seller may take slightly longer depending on the sales region.
- Metering: if you want metered billing (usage-based), we need the metering API implemented and a sandbox account for validation.

We can provide a co-sell pitch deck template and an example Offer listing to speed copy/asset creation. If helpful, I can schedule a technical validation call next week to review the OIDC flow and metering endpoints.

Best,
Miguel Torres
Partner GTM, Azure Marketplace

Team — summarizing the constraints and proposing a recommended mapping for Redwood: 

- Default approach: Keep Starter/Scale/Enterprise as our canonical product tiers (one Offer -> multiple Plans on Azure, one Offer per tier on AWS using Pricing Plan API, one listing on GCP with SKUs per plan).
- Billing model mapping: Starter = seat-based monthly; Scale = seat + usage cap; Enterprise = committed capacity (annual) + enterprise add-ons (SLA, private deployment).
- Regions: Canary in us-east-1 for all markets. Expand to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 after initial 30-day validation.
- Co-sell readiness: collect SSO/OIDC docs, SOC2 summary, legal addendum template, and a 1-page value statement for field sellers.

Marcus — can you provide the 95th percentile latency numbers for us-east-1 and us-west-2 for the inference runtime? Laura — please flag any commercial terms that will block a transactable listing (lead time on invoicing, refund policy, etc.).

If everyone aligns, I'll convert the attached spreadsheet into a marketplace-ready Offer/Plan mapping and submit to AWS first (per Priya's timeline).

Thanks,
